5. Discard this work

Which option?

**A. New PR body (option 1)**

The file writer puts this body at `/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3`:

```markdown
## Summary
- Report an import row's missing id.

## Test Plan
- [x] Reject a row without an id.

## Integration

- before merge - requester: confirm the vendor shipped the fix; done when the vendor's release notes list it
- before deploy to staging - operator: drain the queue; done when the queue length reads 0
  - Keep intake paused during the drain.
- `not stated` - operator: run the cutover; done when `not stated`
- after merge - person merging: tag the release; done when the tag exists
- after deploy to staging - operator: log in through the real identity provider; done when the login succeeds
- after deploy to production - operator: compare the order total; done when it equals the total read before the deploy

Keep these labels on the receipt:

~~~text
EOF
End of receipt
~~~
```

**A. Create command (separate call)**

```bash
(cd '/work/import queue' && LANDED_SUBJECT=$(cat '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3.title') && gh pr create --title "$LANDED_SUBJECT" --body-file '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3')
```

The file writer put the Markdown body in the minted scratch file and the landed subject in its `.title` sibling, and `gh pr create` reads the body through `--body-file`. Because the body and subject come from files, the shell never interprets `$(import)`, the backticks or the `EOF` line.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before and After are identical on this case, so the After wording moved no fact: create and update already hold in Before rather than moving from fails to holds as expected. Both show the five-option menu in order with no Integration question, both carry the Integration block verbatim once after Test Plan with the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines and no checked claims, and both replace only the stale Integration block in the draft while keeping the intro spacing and Notes. The one judgement call is the title: both outputs read it from an unminted `.title` sibling of the body file via `$(cat ...)` into a quoted variable. I counted that as one literal --title argument kept outside shell source, but the rendered command never shows the subject and the sibling path is invented rather than printed by the mint. To make create robust, the wording could say where the landed subject is written (its own minted scratch file, or an explicitly named sibling) and that the create call reads it from there as a single quoted argument, while keeping the current rules: body as data in the minted file, the same printed path passed via --body-file, an explicit cd into the observed worktree, and no reliance on variables from earlier calls.
